landing.heroTitle: The operating system for secondhand goods.
landing.heroTitleHighlight: From intake to sale — everything in one place.
landing.heroDescription: Kivvi understands the difference between a donation, a purchase, and a repair. It tracks every item, calculates condition and value, and measures impact. For thrift stores, IT refurbishers, vintage shops, repair cafés, and everyone giving used things a second life.
landing.originStory: Kivvi was built at revamp-it — one of Switzerland's largest IT refurbishers. Since 2003 they take in electronics, test, repair, and resell them. After years with ERPs that were never designed for secondhand, they built their own. Now it's open source — for all circular economy businesses.
landing.scenario1Text: A company drops off 50 retired laptops. You type '50 Lenovo ThinkPad' and hit enter. 50 items tracked, QR labels ready to print, donation receipt generated.
landing.scenario2Text: Volunteer Maria opens laptop #23. Battery: 78%. Screen: scratch. Condition: Fair. New battery: CHF 40. Logged in 30 seconds — repair costs flow directly into margin calculation.
landing.scenario3Text: Customer walks in. CHF 80 instead of CHF 135 — guide price, adjusted to their budget. Scan QR. Done. Dashboard shows: CHF 30 margin, 25 kg e-waste avoided.
landing.cap6: Swiss QR-bills, VAT, CAMT bank import
landing.ctaDescription: Write to us — whether you run a thrift store, refurbisher, repair café, or vintage shop.
landing.problem1: Know the difference between a donation, a purchase, and a repair
landing.problem2: Track individual items with their own condition, history, and costs
landing.problem3: Accumulate costs across intake → repair → sale
landing.problem4: Automatically generate donation receipts and impact reports
landing.problem5: Handle QR-bills, VAT, and Swiss compliance natively
landing.knowledgeTeaserText: How do you grade condition correctly? What must a donation receipt contain? How do you measure impact? We've worked through these questions — and documented the answers.
